description:
`jit dep add` silently creates a transitively redundant edge, but `jit validate` treats transitive-reduction violations as errors — so the write succeeds now and the repository fails validation later, wherever the next validate happens to run.

## Background

Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2). Adding `a1b6b3da -> 3d9e9222` silently made the pre-existing `9a7106ae -> 3d9e9222` edge redundant; the violation surfaced inside an unrelated issue's code-review gate (which runs validation), costing that issue a review round and a re-run.

The asymmetry is the root friction: acyclicity is enforced at write time (cycle detection runs before every dependency operation, INV-DAG-ACYCLIC), while the transitive-reduction property is enforced only at read/validate time.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit dep add` rejects, with a nonzero exit, an edge that shadows an existing direct edge or is itself made redundant by existing edges, and the error names the offending edge pair. Covered by a test adding such an edge.
- [hard] REQ-02: passing an explicit `--reduce` flag to the same operation makes the add succeed by dropping the now-redundant edge in the same operation, leaving the graph transitively reduced. Covered by a test asserting the shadowed edge is gone and the new edge present.
- [hard] REQ-03: after any `jit dep add`, the repository contains no transitive-reduction violation that a later `jit validate` would report — a silent write followed by a distant validation error is no longer possible.
title: jit dep add allows silently creating transitively redundant edges
